name: Carnegie Mellon University
summary: Carnegie Mellon grew from the Carnegie Technical Schools founded by Andrew Carnegie in 1900 and became Carnegie Mellon University in 1967 after merging with the Mellon Institute. Its School of Computer Science admits undergraduates directly and is far more selective than the university overall. CMU does not award institutional financial aid to international undergraduates.

testing.notes: Fall 2027: required for the School of Computer Science; other colleges are "test flexible" (SAT, ACT, IB, AP, A-level or French Bac results); Fine Arts is test-optional.

internationalTuition.notes: First-years entering fall 2026. Same rate for international students.

livingEstimate.notes: Standard double room US$11,700 plus traditional first-year meal plan US$7,950.

scholarships.name: Need-based aid (US citizens and permanent residents)
scholarships.eligibility: CMU does not award institutional financial aid to international undergraduates; international families must plan to pay the full cost of attendance.

campusAreaAcres.notes: Main campus in Pittsburgh's Oakland neighbourhood.

housing.value: All first-years must live in university housing; housing is guaranteed for four years if students stay in the university system. CMU owns 26 residence halls and apartments.

admissionStats.notes: Early Decision: 2,680 applied, 553 admitted. Admits' middle-50% SAT 1500–1560 (65.5% submitted).

admissionProcess.detail: Apply to a specific CMU college; testing rules differ by college.
Early Decision by 1 November (notified by 15 December) or Regular Decision by 4 January (notified by 1 April).
Non-native speakers send TOEFL or IELTS results by 1 January.
CMU awards no institutional aid to international undergraduates.

feeBreakdown.notes: Total resident cost of attendance US$93,614.
